c-ns-unit.label: Unit digits and cycles
c-ns-unit.summary: Only the last digit of the base matters, and its powers repeat in a short cycle (length 4 at most).

c-ns-rem.label: Remainders and divisibility
c-ns-rem.summary: Work with the remainder, not the big number: use the divisor's rule, or replace powers by their remainders.

c-ns-factors.label: Prime factorisation: factors, squares, trailing zeros
c-ns-factors.summary: Write the number as a product of prime powers; factor counts, perfect-square divisors and zeros all read off the exponents.

c-ns-count.label: Counting numbers in a range
c-ns-count.summary: Find the first and last member of the list, then (last − first) ÷ step + 1.

c-ns-word.label: Number word problems and digit puzzles
c-ns-word.summary: Translate the words to an equation (or to a product of digits) and solve; many are quicker by trying the options.

c-ns-series.label: Series and sums of numbers
c-ns-series.summary: Pair terms, split into APs, or use the standard sums of 1…n, squares and cubes.

q-ns-unit-pow.label: Unit digit of powers and their products
q-ns-unit-pow.summary: A product or sum of big powers; the unit digit is asked.

q-ns-unit-seq.short: Unit digit of a sum or factorial
q-ns-unit-seq.label: Unit digit of a sum or factorial
q-ns-unit-seq.summary: A sum like 1 + 2 + … + n, or n!, with the unit digit asked.

q-ns-rem-chain.label: Remainders when divided successively
q-ns-rem-chain.summary: A number divided first by one divisor and then its quotient by the next; remainders are given or asked.

q-ns-rem-large.label: Remainder of a very large number or sum of powers
q-ns-rem-large.summary: A long number, a sum of powers or a prime, divided by a small number.

q-ns-nearest.label: Least or nearest number divisible by a given number
q-ns-nearest.summary: Least n-digit number divisible by k, or the multiple of k nearest to a given number.

q-ns-div-rule.label: What must a number or expression be divisible by
q-ns-div-rule.summary: A digit-sum difference, or a sum of two big powers, and the divisors it always has.

q-ns-factors.label: Count factors, square divisors or find the largest prime factor
q-ns-factors.summary: Factorise an expression, then count with (power + 1) or find its biggest prime.

q-ns-zeros.label: Number of zeros at the end of a product
q-ns-zeros.summary: Count the pairs of 2 and 5 in a product of numbers or powers.

q-ns-count.label: How many numbers satisfy a digit or remainder condition
q-ns-count.summary: Numbers ending in a digit, leaving a remainder, or between two roots.

q-ns-word.label: Number word problems (consecutive, sum and difference, primes)
q-ns-word.summary: Consecutive odd numbers, fractions of groups, sum and difference of squares, a rational between two fractions, primes that add up to a total.

q-ns-digit-puzzle.label: Digit puzzles: repeating decimals and digit products
q-ns-digit-puzzle.summary: xy ÷ ab = 0.xyxy…, or digits of a product that follow a rule.

q-ns-series.label: Sum of a series or of the digits of a sum
q-ns-series.summary: Alternating pairs, two interleaved APs, 5 + 55 + 555…, a sum of cubes, a geometric-looking decimal series.

formulas.note: Exponent mod 4 (use 4 when the remainder is 0).

formulas.text: Remainder on dividing by d₁ × d₂ after successive remainders r₁, r₂:  d₁ × r₂ + r₁
formulas.note: For three divisors work from the back: N = d₁(d₂(d₃q + r₃) + r₂) + r₁.

formulas.text: 2^n, 5^n: look at the last n digits.  Divisible by 16 → last 4 digits.  By 9 → digit sum.  By 11 → (sum of odd places) − (sum of even places)
formulas.note: A number minus its digit sum is always a multiple of 9.

formulas.text: N = p^a × q^b × r^c  →  number of factors = (a + 1)(b + 1)(c + 1).  Perfect-square factors = (⌊a/2⌋ + 1)(⌊b/2⌋ + 1)…
formulas.note: Factorise before anything else; take out the common power.

formulas.text: Trailing zeros = the smaller of (count of 2s, count of 5s). For n!: ⌊n/5⌋ + ⌊n/25⌋ + ⌊n/125⌋ + …
formulas.note: There are almost always more 2s, so count 5s.

formulas.text: Count of multiples / numbers in an AP = (last − first) ÷ step + 1
formulas.note: Find the first and last member inside the limits first. Digits: the first place cannot be 0.
1 + 11 + 111 + … (n terms) is a string of 1s added in columns.

formulas.text: Nearest multiple of d to N: remainder r = N mod d. Down: N − r. Up: N + (d − r). Choose the smaller shift.
formulas.note: r < d ÷ 2 means go down. Least n-digit number: start from 10^(n−1) and go up.

formulas.text: x² − y² = (x + y)(x − y).   0.̅a̅b̅ (repeating block) = ab ÷ 99
formulas.note: Sum and the difference of squares give the difference in one division.

q-ns-unit-pow.cue: 'Unit digit of …' with a power, a product of powers or a sum of powers.
q-ns-unit-pow.standard: Keep only the last digit of each base. Find its cycle, reduce the exponent mod 4 (0 → 4), read the unit digit, then combine the unit digits by multiplying or adding and keep the last digit again.
q-ns-unit-pow.fast: Bases ending in 0, 1, 5, 6 never change; for 4 and 9 only the odd/even exponent matters; for 2, 3, 7, 8 use exponent mod 4.
q-ns-unit-pow.eliminate: Parity and the last digit of a product of unit digits rule out options: an even base with a positive exponent gives an even unit digit.
traps: Using the exponent itself instead of exponent mod 4.
Using remainder 0 as 'the first value' when it is the fourth.
Forgetting that the sum of two unit digits can carry to a second digit; keep only the last.

q-ns-unit-seq.cue: Unit digit of 1 + 2 + … + n, or of n!.
q-ns-unit-seq.standard: For a sum use n(n + 1)/2 and read its last digit. For a factorial: from 5! onwards a 2 and a 5 are both present, so the unit digit is 0.
q-ns-unit-seq.fast: n! for n ≥ 5 always ends in 0; no calculation needed.
q-ns-unit-seq.eliminate: For n! with n ≥ 5 only the option 0 can be right.
traps: Computing n! for small n and carrying that digit.
Adding the digits instead of using the formula.

q-ns-rem-chain.standard: Rebuild the number from the last remainder backwards, take the smallest value, and then divide it again in the order asked.
q-ns-rem-chain.fast: For two divisors: remainder on the product = d₁ × r₂ + r₁.
q-ns-rem-chain.eliminate: The remainder on dividing by d₁d₂ must be less than d₁d₂ and leave remainder r₁ when divided by d₁ (59 mod 8 = 3).
traps: Dividing in the wrong order after reversing.
Using the quotient as if it were the number.

q-ns-rem-large.cue: 'Remainder when [a huge number / sum of powers / the smallest 4-digit prime] is divided by …'
q-ns-rem-large.standard: Replace the number by something small with the same remainder: last digits for 2, 4, 5, 8, 16; each power by its remainder; a sum by the sum of the remainders.
q-ns-rem-large.fast: For 16 take the last four digits; for sums of powers find what each term leaves and count the terms.
q-ns-rem-large.eliminate: The remainder is always smaller than the divisor, so large options are out at once.
traps: Taking too few last digits (16 needs four).
Forgetting to reduce the sum of remainders again.

q-ns-nearest.cue: 'Least n-digit number divisible by …' or 'number nearest to … divisible by …'
q-ns-nearest.standard: Divide the target by the divisor, look at the remainder, and add (divisor − remainder) to go up or subtract the remainder to go down.
q-ns-nearest.fast: Compare the remainder with half the divisor to choose up or down.
q-ns-nearest.eliminate: Only options divisible by the divisor survive; a quick last-digit check removes some.
traps: Adding the remainder instead of divisor − remainder.
Using the product of the primes with a wrong digit.

q-ns-div-rule.cue: '… is always divisible by', 'the expression … is divisible by'
q-ns-div-rule.standard: Write the number as an algebraic expression (100m + 10n + k) or factorise the bases (333 = 3 × 3 × 37), then see which factors always appear.
q-ns-div-rule.fast: A number minus its digit sum is a multiple of 9.
q-ns-div-rule.eliminate: Test two different numbers: any option that fails once is out.
traps: Stopping at the first divisor that works when 'all of these' is an option.

q-ns-factors.cue: 'How many positive factors', 'perfect squares that divide', 'largest prime factor'
q-ns-factors.standard: Take out the common power, factorise each part into primes and use (power + 1) for factors; squares need even exponents.
q-ns-factors.fast: 9^8 + 9^9 + 9^10 + 9^11 = 9^8 × 820: the bracket is small and easy to factorise.
q-ns-factors.eliminate: Number of factors of 3^16 alone is already 17, so any option below 17 is out.
traps: Counting power instead of power + 1.
Counting all factors instead of only square ones.

q-ns-zeros.cue: 'Number of zeros at the end of the product / expression'
q-ns-zeros.standard: Count the 2s and the 5s in the prime factorisation; the smaller count is the number of zeros.
q-ns-zeros.fast: A power k^k with k a multiple of 5 gives k fives (extra k for multiples of 25).
q-ns-zeros.eliminate: Zeros can't exceed the count of either 2s or 5s.
traps: Counting 10s as a separate factor without also counting its 2 and 5.
Counting only the multiples of 5 and missing the extra 5 in 25, 50, 75, 100.

q-ns-count.cue: 'How many numbers between … that end in / leave remainder / are divisible by …'
q-ns-count.standard: List the first and last number that qualify inside the limits, then (last − first) ÷ step + 1.
q-ns-count.fast: A digit in the units place repeats every 10; a remainder condition repeats every divisor.
q-ns-count.eliminate: The count can't exceed (upper − lower) ÷ step + 1.
traps: Including the endpoints that are not in the list.
Allowing 0 as the first digit.

q-ns-word.cue: A number story: consecutive numbers, fractions of groups, sum/difference of squares, a rational between two fractions, primes that add up.
q-ns-word.standard: Name the unknown, write the condition as an equation and solve; or test the options.
q-ns-word.fast: Sum and difference of squares: difference = (difference of squares) ÷ sum.
q-ns-word.eliminate: For parity and size, strike options that break them first.
traps: Taking the first number when the second was asked.
Stopping at a prime test without checking the largest option.

q-ns-digit-puzzle.cue: xy ÷ ab = 0.xyxy…, or a digit rule on a product.
q-ns-digit-puzzle.standard: A repeating block of two digits is that block ÷ 99. For a digit rule try a couple of small values of x and y.
q-ns-digit-puzzle.fast: Try each option once on a simple xy.
q-ns-digit-puzzle.eliminate: An option that fails for one test pair is out.
traps: Using 100 instead of 99 for a repeating two-digit block.

q-ns-series.cue: 'Sum of the first … terms', '5 + 55 + 555…', alternating or interleaved sequences.
q-ns-series.standard: Spot the structure first: pairs that add to a constant, two interleaved APs, a string of 1s, or a sum of cubes.
q-ns-series.eliminate: Check the sign and the size of the first few terms to remove options.
traps: Misjudging the number of pairs.
Forgetting to remove 1³ when the sum starts at 2.

pyqs.text: The expression 333^555 + 555^333 is divisible by:
solution: 333 = 3 × 111 = 3 × 3 × 37 and 555 = 5 × 111 = 3 × 5 × 37: both numbers are multiples of 3 and of 37.
So both powers are multiples of 3 and of 37, and so is their sum.
One power is odd and the other is odd, so the sum is even: divisible by 2 as well. All three divide it.
pyqs.trick: Both bases are multiples of 111 = 3 × 37; odd + odd is even. All three divide it.
